title: Predictive token-burst kernel selector with hardware telemetry fusion
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Implement a predictive kernel selection component that uses short-horizon token-burst forecasts plus fused GPU/CPU telemetry to choose an execution kernel (and quantization variant) per request. The goal is to reduce 95th/99th tail latency regressions and unit cost for mixed conversational workloads by making prefill vs decode kernel choices anticipatory rather than reactive.

Motivation and context: Current kernel picker is mostly policy/heuristic-driven and reacts to observed sequence length during prefill and decode. For workloads with sudden token bursts (e.g., multi-turn assistants, long code completions), this reactive switching leads to extra context copy/rewarm, pipeline stalls, or choosing a conservative kernel that hurts median latency. We believe short-horizon prediction (50-200 token window) fused with runtime telemetry (SM utilization, memory pressure, temperature/hotspots) can meaningfully improve kernel choice and reduce costly fallback events.

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce 95th latency for mixed conversational workloads by >= 10% in our staging tests.
- Reduce frequency of mid-request kernel fallback events by >= 40%.
- Keep median latency change within +/-3%.
- No increase in GPU OOM incidents in canary clusters.
- Validate cost/per-token delta for selected kernels (report per-model ROI).

High-level design:
1) Token-burst predictor: lightweight classifier that consumes request-level metadata and prefix tokens statistics (token types, user prompt length, user-intent signal where available) to predict whether a burst is likely within next N tokens. The model must be tiny (<50KB on-disk) and run in the serving path with <200 microseconds 99th latency.
2) Telemetry fusion layer: sliding-window aggregation of low-overhead GPU telemetry (SM utilization, active CPI proxy, device mem headroom), CPU event loop lag, and request queuing time. Telemetry is sampled at ~100ms and maintained per-executor warm cache.
3) Decision policy: combine prediction + telemetry into a cost-aware score that selects: (a) prefill-optimized kernel, (b) decode-optimized kernel, or (c) quantized fallback kernel. Score includes latency risk, token cost delta, and safety margin based on current cluster load.
4) Online learner: A bandit-style updater observes realized latency & cost per decision and nudges decision thresholds asynchronously. Must be conservative (small step sizes) to avoid instability.
5) Safety & rollback: any kernel switch that increases tail latency during a rolling canary triggers a rollback with automatic throttle.

Technical constraints & trade-offs:
- Prediction model accuracy vs inference overhead: we prioritize tiny models to limit added CPU latency. Heavier models can be used offline to generate policies.
- Telemetry staleness: sampling interval and aggregation window tuned to balance noise vs responsiveness.
- Quantized kernels provide cost savings but might degrade quality; must be restricted to models with verified quantization profiles.
- Must be compatible with private deployments: telemetry collection must be optional and work with customer-provided metrics sinks or limited telemetry.

Plan & milestones:
- Week 1 (Feb 12–18): Spec, evaluation harness, synthetic burst dataset generation and baseline.
- Week 2: Implement token-burst predictor prototype + local microbench harness.
- Week 3: Telemetry aggregator + decision policy implementation; offline simulation against production traces.
- Week 4: Integrate online learner and safety hooks; unit/e2e tests.
- Week 5: Canary rollout to staging canary cohort (10% of staging traffic).
- Week 6: Evaluate canary, iterate thresholds, expand to internal prod small-scale canary (1 region).

Rollout strategy: start with model families labelled "burst-safe" in model-catalog. Use per-route opt-in flags. Canary monitor checks: tail-latency SLOs, fallback-rate, OOMs, quality regression. If any threshold crossed, automatic rollback to baseline policy for that route.

Evaluation datasets and harness: will reuse runtime trace replays (trace-2024-q4-bursts.tar) and generate adversarial bursts from real chat logs (sanitized). Local microbench will emulate GPU telemetry patterns.

Implementation notes: prefer Rust runtime module with a thin C ABI to the runtime scheduler. Predictor can be a tiny decision tree or GLM compiled to a fast table lookup. Decision policy will be parameterized by weights in a small JSON config stored per-deployment.

Open questions:
- How to expose predictor inputs/outputs in APM dashboards? (required for debugging).
- Limits for telemetry sampling in Private deployments.
- Guardrails for models without validated quantization profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Predictor integrated into runtime and measurable in staging replay harness
95th latency improvement >= 10% on mixed conversational trace suite
Fallback events reduced by >= 40% on replayed traces
Canary rollout with automatic rollback working end-to-end
No increase in GPU OOM incidents during canary
